title: Recover the live terminal connection automatically without losing unsent text
prompt:
When a window's live terminal output disconnects, LocalRuntimeNotice (src/components/LocalRuntimeNotice.tsx) shows a notice and waits for the person to press Reconnect. Delayed events can latch an obsolete failure, and the reload after a reconnect throws away unsent composer text. Make the recovery automatic and bounded. Recovery reloads the document, so unsent local text has to survive that reload. Saving the text across the reload is only safe once you can tell local tabs from cloud ones, and once cloud drafts have been saved by their own account-scoped cache.

Behaviour of `LocalRuntimeNotice({ reload })`, which uses `localRuntime.status()` and `localRuntime.reconnect()` from src/lib/api.ts and listens to `local_runtime_disconnected`, `local_runtime_view_disconnected` and `local_runtime_reattached`:
- A disconnect event triggers a fresh `status()` read. The notice (role "status", showing the status message under a "Live connection unavailable" heading) appears only if the current status is unavailable. Another window's failure, or a delayed event while the transport is healthy, shows nothing. An older status reply never overwrites a newer failure. Focus never moves.
- While unavailable, it reconnects automatically after 1 s, 2 s and 4 s, at most three times per window lifetime, across reloads and remounts. Keep the count in src/lib/localRuntimeRecovery.ts: `RECOVERY_DELAYS = [1000, 2000, 4000]`, `recoveryAttempts()` and `recordRecoveryAttempt()`, stored in sessionStorage under `terminalx.localRuntime.attempts.v1`. An unreadable or invalid value counts as exhausted, and the attempt is recorded before the reconnect is issued. Attempts are never replenished automatically.
- After the automatic attempts, a "Reconnect" button retries by hand. It shows "Reconnecting…" and is disabled while a retry runs. Clicks during a pending health read collapse into exactly one retry. Health is still checked every 5 s, and the notice clears without a reload if the runtime recovers on its own.
- A successful reconnect, or a `local_runtime_reattached` event, reloads once. If a newer disconnect arrived while a reconnect was in flight, it reads status again instead of reloading. A reattached event while the status is connected reloads without reconnecting.
- Unmounting cancels timers and listeners and ignores any reply still in flight.

Before any reload, checkpoint unsent local drafts:
- In src/lib/drafts.ts add `checkpointDraftsForRecovery(localTabIds: Iterable<string>)`. It writes only those tabs' drafts to sessionStorage `terminalx.localRuntime.localDrafts.v2` as a JSON array of `[tabId, text]` pairs. A storage failure throws.
- When the module loads, it restores that checkpoint once and removes it. It also removes the legacy `terminalx.localRuntime.drafts.v1` without restoring anything from it, because that format mixed cloud drafts in.
- Local tab ids come from `getSessionStore()` in src/lib/sessions.ts (its `sessions[].tabs[].id`). Wait to reload until the store is `loaded`.
- Also wait until `cloudDraftsReadyForRecovery()` from src/lib/cloudAgents.ts returns true. Add it there: it is true only when every cloud tab draft has been acknowledged by the account-scoped cache.
- If the checkpoint cannot be stored, do not reload. Keep the text in memory and show the error message in the notice.
notes:
Source: PR #645, six commits; the last only edits CHANGELOG.md.
Chain: a2a7fae5 rewrites LocalRuntimeNotice.tsx for health-checked, bounded automatic recovery (and its Rust side in local_runtime/ui.rs and desktop.rs). 43ee3d7e changes that same component to checkpoint drafts before the reload, adding src/lib/localRuntimeRecovery.ts and a draft checkpoint in drafts.ts. d3b0a297 narrows the drafts.ts checkpoint to identified local tabs (v2 key, legacy v1 dropped) and changes the component to pass them. 269f6c3a adds cloudDraftsReadyForRecovery to cloudAgents.ts and has the component wait for it. d05ef195 reworks the cloud cache mutation ordering in cloudAgents.ts that this readiness depends on.
Each step edits what the one before it added.
Replaying only the PR's own commits onto startCommit passes the check, so it does not depend on what main merged into the branch.
The check is the PR's LocalRuntimeNotice.test.tsx, which mocks cloudAgents. The PR's cloudAgents.account.test.ts cache-ordering cases are left out. The Rust half is not checked.
